chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the woman when her husband divorces her, when does she become in control of herself? He said: When she sees the blood of the third menstruation, then she is in control of herself. I said: And if the blood hastens to her before the days of her period? He said: If the blood is before ten days, then he is in control of her, and it is from the menstruation from which she was purified; and if the blood is after the ten days, then it is from the third menstruation, and she is in control of herself.

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِنَفْسِهَا: She is in control of herself (regarding the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: When does a divorced woman regain control of her waiting period according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the precise mechanism of 'takhliyah' (freeing the wife from the husband's option) in a revocable divorce by anchoring the legal status to the physiological reality of menstruation. It demonstrates the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between 'hayd' (menstruation) and 'istihaDAH' (irregular bleeding) based on the ten-day threshold, thereby determining when the husband's right of retraction expires. This ruling ensures that the woman's autonomy is restored only after the completion of the third distinct menstrual cycle, aligning with the Quranic mandate for a clear, observable end to the waiting period.
